sections.label: Major workplace injuries in Singapore
sections.summary: Singapore recorded 660 major workplace injuries in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In 2025, Singapore recorded 660 major workplace injuries.

sections.label: Ontario and Germany return-to-work practices
sections.summary: Ontario's board returns nine in 10 injured workers to work within a year, and Germany requires reintegration processes after six weeks' absence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In Ontario, Canada, nine in 10 injured workers supported by the Workplace Safety and Insurance Board return to work within a year through customised support and clear employer obligations to provide suitable work and accommodations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In Germany, employers are required to offer structured reintegration processes for workers who have been absent for more than six weeks within a 12-month period.

sections.label: SMEs share of local workforce
sections.summary: SMEs employ around 70% of Singapore's local workforce today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: SMEs employ around 70% of our local workforce today.

sections.label: Proposed Back-to-Work pathway
sections.summary: The speaker proposes a dedicated Back-to-Work pathway for workers unable to return to previous jobs due to illness or injury.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: By drawing inspiration from these programmes, I propose that we develop a dedicated Back-to-Work pathway that supports workers who are unable to return to their previous jobs due to illness or injury.

sections.label: Time-bound wage support scheme proposal
sections.summary: The speaker suggests a time-bound wage support scheme to help employers reintegrate workers recovering from serious health conditions, noting no dedicated funding mechanism exists.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: This is a direction I hope Singapore should aspire to move towards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I therefore suggest that the Government consider introducing a time-bound wage support scheme to help employers reintegrate workers recovering from serious health conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Unlike support for persons with disabilities, there is currently no dedicated funding mechanism to incentivise employers to provide workplace accommodations for workers returning to work after serious non-work-related illnesses or medical conditions.

sections.label: MediSave for return-to-work expenses
sections.summary: The passage proposes allowing MediSave use for return-to-work-related expenses such as assessments of a worker's condition and fitness for work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Allowing MediSave to be used for return-to-work-related expenses, such as assessments and evaluations of a worker's condition and fitness for work.

sections.label: Unemployed residents leaving jobs for health
sections.summary: Survey data shows about 3,800 unemployed residents on average over five years left previous jobs for health-related reasons.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
sentences.text: Our survey data shows that on average, over the past five years, there were about 3,800 unemployed residents who had left their previous jobs due to health-related reasons.

sections.label: Pilot workers returning to work
sections.summary: A pilot enrolled 3,700 workers, and coordinators' workflows and support orchestration enabled 95% to return to work successfully.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
sentences.text: The pilot enrolled a total of 3,700 workers whose employers were committed to supporting their participation in the programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
sentences.text: It was found that the workflows managed by the coordinators and their orchestration of support enabled 95% of these workers to successfully return to work.

sections.label: Bounce Back Lab pilot
sections.summary: The Ministry of Health rolled out an inter-agency pilot called the Bounce Back Lab from 2023 to 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
sentences.text: To this end, the Ministry of Health rolled out an inter-agency pilot called the "Bounce Back Lab" from 2023 to 2025.

sections.label: Review and AfA-SHEL launch
sections.summary: The Ministry will review Singapore's return-to-work landscape and launch AfA-SHEL with NTUC and SNEF in the second half of 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
sentences.text: The Ministry will be conducting a review of the return-to-work landscape in Singapore and will consider the Member's suggestions carefully.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
sentences.text: As announced at the Committee of Supply debate last month, we will be launching an Alliance for Action on Safety and Health for Employment Longevity (AfA-SHEL) together with NTUC and SNEF in the second half of 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
sentences.text: The AfA-SHEL will catalyse ground-up solutions to common workplace safety risks and concerns, and facilitating injured workers back to work is one of our focus areas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
sentences.text: Drawing from the lessons from the previous pilots with hospitals, as well as the Bounce Back Lab pilot, proposals could include innovative job redesign approaches for common injuries or health conditions, initiatives to build SMEs' capabilities in supporting return-to-work, or new partnership models that better match workers to jobs, based on their functional abilities.
